newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solvay finalises Bulgarian Sodi deal.
newsitem.headline: Solvay finalises Bulgarian Sodi deal.

text.p: Belgian chemicals and drugs group Solvay SA said on Tuesday it had finalised its purchase of 60 percent in Bulgarian soda ash producer Sodi from the Bulgarian Privatisation Agency.
Solvay said in a statement the remaining shares in Sodi would be offered to Bulgarian investors through a mass privatisation programme and to Sodi staff.

The deal with the privatisation agency is worth $160 million. Solvay said it would "share the acquisition" with Turkish glass and chemicals maker Sisecam and the London-based European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
Sisecam and the EBRD would "buy their participation" through an Austria-based holding company controlled by Solvay.
Solvay gave no details of the size of the stakes the two would hold or their contribution to the purchasing cost.

Solvay would take up 75 percent of Sodi's soda ash production and Sisecam 25 percent. With yearly capacity of 1.2 million tonnes of sodium carbonate -- used among other things in glass, detergents, water and fumes treatment -- Sodi is the world's largest synthetic soda ash plant.

Solvay and the Privatisation Agency also agreed on an investment programme, the long-term supply of limestone and salt as raw material and of steam and electricity, as well as the use of the Varna harbour, near Devnya, where Sodi is located.
The investment will focus on increasing capacity, plant modernisation and environmental improvements.
Solvay said that through the acquisition it would gain access to emerging markets in the Balkans, the Middle East and Central Asia.
